title: Verified: the other session is right, margin is not what makes the maker profitable, the shape of the parlay is. On 6,471 graded parlays, shape explains 8.0% of the spread in per-parlay maker profit and margin only 0.7%. A bad shape stays at -8% to -15% at every margin up to +3 points (a leg over 80%: -13.6% at +0 and -10.4% at +2). In the good class (2 legs, no leg over 80%) each point of margin just loses auctions: at -1 / +0.1 / +1 point we win 95% / 65% / 13% of them and expect +5.3% / +4.4% / +1.0% of the pot per request, while the profit per fill is the class's edge almost regardless of margin. So the engine stays at the thinnest margin (about 0.1 point over our fair) and I did not raise it anywhere. Two more settings now follow the data: it skips parlays our fair puts under 25% to win (+1.7% for $9.61 of locked collateral per $1 staked, against +8.9% for $2.16 on the rest), and the extra 2% on same-game pairs is gone (it cut the auctions we win from 49% to 29% at the same return). Same caveat as before: three slates, so these are best estimates, and a daily readout now repeats the margin test. Details: research/parlay_profit_profile_2026-11-20.md section 5.
